content:
Patterns are the reasoning heart of the Class 4 Olympiad — number sequences, growing patterns and letter codes that reward rule-spotting. This guide covers what the Maths Olympiad Class 4 patterns chapter tests, how to crack each type, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Patterns chapter tests

  • Number patterns with constant and growing steps
  • Doubling/halving and square-number patterns
  • Shape and letter patterns
  • Simple coding rules

Key facts your child should know

  • Write the differences between terms — a constant step or a growing step jumps out.
  • 3, 6, 12, 24 doubles each time; 1, 4, 9, 16 are square numbers.
  • For letter patterns, count the alphabet steps (A→C is +2).
  • Apply the SAME rule from the solved pair to the asked pair.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Continuing by the wrong feature (colour vs shape).
  • Missing that the step itself grows (+1, +2, +3, …).
  • Counting alphabet steps inclusively.

quiz.title: IMO Class 4 Patterns Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: In a 3×3 magic square, the centre number is 9. What is the magic sum of each row, column and diagonal?
questions.explanation: In every 3×3 magic square the magic sum is 3 times the centre number: 3 × 9 = 27.

questions.q: A 3×3 magic square uses each of the numbers 3 to 11 exactly once. What is the magic sum of each row, column and diagonal?
questions.explanation: The total of all nine numbers is 63; divided among 3 rows, each row sums to 21.

questions.q: A growing pattern of dots has 2, 7, 12, 17 dots in its first four figures. How many dots will the 5th figure have?
A pattern repeats: A, B, B, A, B, B, … What is the 10th letter?
questions.explanation: The block A,B,B has length 3. 10 = 3×3 + 1, so the 10th letter starts a new block: A.
The pattern adds 12 each time, so the missing term is 38.

questions.q: A pattern starts at 1 and adds 8 each time (1, 9, 17, …). What is the 11th term?
A pattern starts at 7 and adds 3 each time (7, 10, 13, …). What is the 12th term?

questions.explanation: The pattern adds 11 each time, so the missing term is 19.

questions.q: Tara counts down from 100 in steps of 8: 100, 92, 84, … Which of these numbers will she say?
questions.explanation: Every number said differs from 100 by a multiple of 8; 100 − 8 × 6 = 52, so 52 is said.

faq.q: How do you find a number pattern rule?
faq.a: Subtract neighbouring terms. Equal differences mean a constant step; growing differences mean the step increases each time.
17 — the steps are +1, +2, +3, +4, so the next step is +5.
